docs.title: mlflow-experience
docs.text:
A simple, configuration-driven MLOps pipeline built with Scikit-Learn, Pydantic, and MLflow.

Welcome to mlflow-experience! This project lets you build, train, evaluate, and track machine learning experiments without writing boilerplate code. Instead of editing Python scripts every time you want to try a new feature, a different scaler, or a new model, you define your experiment in a YAML configuration file.

docs.title: Why Use This Project?
docs.text:
1. No Manual Glue Code: Define your data source, preprocessing steps, model type, and hyperparameters in YAML.
  2. No Data Leakage: Transformations (like scalers, encoders, and imputers) learn their parameters only on the training set and apply them safely to the test set.
  3. DataFrames Stay DataFrames: We use Scikit-Learn's transform_output="pandas" so column names are never lost during preprocessing.
  4. Automatic MLflow Tracking: Your hyperparameters, evaluation metrics, model files, and console logs are automatically saved to MLflow.
  5. Type Safety with Pydantic: Your YAML configuration is checked before running. If a column name is missing or a strategy typo exists, it fails immediately with a clear error.

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
Here is how simple an experiment looks in YAML:

# configs/mvp.yaml (snippet)
dataset:
  train:
    type: csv
    path: data/raw/churn_train.csv
    target_column: Churn
    id_column: CustomerID

preprocessing:
  - name: handle_missing
    type: missing
    params:
      columns:
        - name: Age
          strategy: mean

  - name: scale_features
    type: scaling
    params:
      columns:
        - name: Age
          strategy: standard

model:
  type: logistic_regression
  task: 'binary:classification'
  hyperparameters:
    max_iter: 250

Run this in your terminal:

uv run python -m main --config configs/mvp.yaml

The pipeline loads the data, cleans missing values, scales features, fits a logistic regression model, evaluates accuracy and F1 score, and logs the run to MLflow.

docs.title: Codebase Audit: Complexity, Code Smells & Maintainability
docs.text: Audit Date: October 2026 Auditor: Staff+ Software Engineer Repository: sid-146/mlflow-experience Target: Full Repository Architecture, Code Quality, Observability & Reliability Artifact Path: docs/CODEBASE_AUDIT.md

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: This codebase audit presents a comprehensive, evidence-based evaluation of mlflow-experience, a declarative, configuration-driven MLOps pipeline designed to orchestrate tabular data preprocessing, model fitting, and MLflow tracking via YAML specifications.

docs.title: Key Takeaways
docs.text:
1. Compelling Conceptual Foundation with Execution Flaws: The project exhibits a solid architectural philosophy—decoupling pipeline orchestration into 5 logical layers and enforcing schema validation via Pydantic. However, the runtime implementation contains critical correctness bugs, severed contracts between validation and execution, and unfinished prototypes that undermine its declarative promises.

  2. Critical Evaluation Defect (CORR-001): In src/orchestrator.py:78, the holdout test data references are overwritten with the training set (self.data_loader.X_test, self.data_loader.y_test = x_train, y_train). Consequently, all test evaluations are computed on the training set, concealing overfitting and producing invalid validation metrics.

  3. Incomplete MLflow Observability (ARCH-002): While marketed as an automated MLflow tracking framework, Orchestrator never invokes mlflow_tracker.log_metrics(), mlflow_tracker.log_params(), mlflow_tracker.log_model(), or mlflow_tracker.end_run(). It only uploads the plaintext runtime log file upon exit.

  4. Zero Test Coverage (TEST-001): The repository contains no unit, integration, or regression tests. Neither pytest nor any test runner is declared in requirements.txt or pyproject.toml.

  5. Contract Drift & Dead Features: Pydantic policies accept types (parquet, xlsx) that crash at runtime in DataLoader, while runtime code supports formats (json) that Pydantic rejects. Preprocessing steps such as cleaning and filter crash at initialization because their policy mapping is None.

docs.title: Module Boundary Analysis
docs.text:
• Tight Coupling to RunContext: Almost every class (DataLoader, DataSplitter, PreprocessingPipeline, MLflowTracker, Orchestrator) takes the monolithic RunContext God Object. Internal components reach deep into nested sub-contexts, violating encapsulation.
  • Missing Boundaries: src/core/models/linear.py contains an abandoned build_model() function, while the actual model builder resides in src/core/pipelines/model_builder.py.

docs.title: 1. PreprocessingPipeline._instantiate_transformer() (src/core/pipelines/preprocessing.py:16-37)
docs.text:
• Nature of Complexity: Ad-hoc introspection and branching based on attribute presence (hasattr(params, "mapping"), hasattr(params, "columns"), hasattr(params, "dict")).
  • Consequence: Fragile instantiation logic that fails silently or falls back to empty constructors when new policies do not match hardcoded attribute checks.

docs.title: 2. MissingValueTransformer.fit() (src/core/pipelines/transformers.py:54-84)
docs.text:
• Nature of Complexity: Flagged by the author with # Todo: Improve this function. Too complex. Nested conditionals handle both policy objects and legacy dictionary structures, applying column-specific aggregations across heterogenous strategies (mean, median, mode, constant).
  • Consequence: High cyclomatic complexity; mixing numeric and categorical data paths without column type guards causes runtime exceptions when mean is mistakenly applied to strings.

docs.title: 3. EncodingTransformer.build() (src/core/pipelines/transformers.py:210-241)
docs.text:
• Nature of Complexity: Manually collects and groups columns by strategy into dictionaries, attempts to track category ordering in a detached list, and instantiates nested Scikit-Learn ColumnTransformer instances.
  • Consequence: Column order configuration is lost, while unmapped strategies produce warnings but proceed to build partial pipelines.

docs.title: 1. Reliance on Global Variable Scope (main.py:10-12, 35-37)
docs.text:
main.py defines run(*args, **kwargs) but accesses the global variable config assigned in the __main__ block: 

def run(*args, **kwargs):
    context = RunContext.from_yaml_dict(
        config
    )  # 'config' is unresolved in function scope!


...
if __name__ == "__main__":
    config = config_loader(args.config)
    run(**config)
Problem: run() unpacks **config into kwargs, but completely ignores kwargs and accesses config from the module global scope. Any programmatic invocation of run() from a script or test suite crashes with NameError: name 'config' is not defined.

docs.title: 2. Fragile Logger Handler Indexing (src/orchestrator.py:169)
docs.text:
In Orchestrator.__exit__: 

self.mlflow_tracker.log_artifact(
    console.handlers[1].baseFilename,
    f"logs/{self.mlflow_tracker.run.info.run_name}.log",
)
Problem: Direct index access (handlers[1]) violates the Law of Demeter. It presumes that console.handlers will always have at least two handlers and that index 1 is unconditionally a FileHandler. If log configuration changes or a handler is removed, this raises IndexError or AttributeError.

docs.title: 3. Side Effects on Module Import (src/core/logging/logger.py:40-54)
docs.text:
Importing logger.py executes: 

LOG_DIR = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "logs")
os.makedirs(LOG_DIR, exist_ok=True)
filename = f"logs_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y_%m_%d_%H_%M')}.log"
filepath = os.path.join(LOG_DIR, filename)
f_handler = logging.FileHandler(filepath, mode="a")
Problem: Merely importing the module creates a new physical file on disk inside src/core/logs/. This has polluted the source repository with over 50 timestamped .log files.

docs.title: 4. Broken Class Definition (src/core/errors/handler_errors.py:1-2)
docs.text:
class LoaderError(BaseException):
    raise
Problem: A bare raise statement is positioned inside the class body. Importing this file raises an immediate RuntimeError: No active exception to reraise. Furthermore, inheriting from BaseException bypasses standard Exception catching.

docs.title: 5. Abandoned & Dead Code Files
docs.text: The repository contains numerous orphaned, unused, or duplicate files: - src/core/pipelines/temp_column_transformer.py: Redundant implementation of column transformations using bare print() statements. - src/core/pipelines/temp_feature_engineering.md: An 8.3 KB design draft committed directly inside the Python source package. - src/core/pipelines/pipeline.py: Unused BasePipeline abstract class. - src/core/pipelines/features.py: Empty 2-line placeholder. - src/core/models/linear.py: Unused prototype returning LinearRegression. - src/utils/data_loader.py: Empty 0-byte file. - src/core/trackers/mlflow_tracker.py:63-160: Nearly 100 lines of commented-out code.

docs.title: 1. Broken Preprocessing Validation Contract
docs.text:
src/core/context/contexts.py:85-87 strictly requires every preprocessing step to map to a valid policy_class: 

def cast_params(self):
    policy_class = self.type.policy_class
    if policy_class is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported preprocessing type: {self.type}")
    self.params = policy_class(**self.params)
However, in src/core/constants/registry.py:52-53: 
PreprocessingRegistry.cleaning: None,
PreprocessingRegistry.filter: None,
Impact: Any configuration containing cleaning or filter steps fails Pydantic schema validation at startup, rendering these implemented transformers unusable.

docs.title: 2. Disconnected Model & Task Mappings
docs.text:
In src/core/constants/registry.py:77-83: 

class ModelType(str, Enum):
    logistic_regression = "logistic_regression"
    random_forest = "random_forest"
    xgboost = "xgboost"

    @property
    def model_class(self):
        mapping = {
            ModelType.logistic_regression: LogisticRegression,
            ModelType.random_forest: None,
            ModelType.xgboost: XGBClassifier,
        }
        return mapping.get(self)
- Specifying random_forest in YAML passes validation but raises ValueError: Given mode : random_forest is not configured yet at runtime. - The pipeline hardcodes Scikit-Learn classifiers and metric evaluations, yet ModelContext contains arbitrary string fields (task: "binary:classification") and TrainingContext contains objective: "binary:logistic" that are completely ignored by ModelBuilder.

docs.title: 3. Divergent File Type Contracts
docs.text:
There is an unresolved contradiction across three files regarding supported dataset formats: - src/core/constants/constants.py:3-8: FILE_TYPES = Literal["csv", "parquet", "excel", "xlsx"] - src/core/constants/registry.py:28-32: {"csv": pd.read_csv, "excel": pd.read_excel, "json": pd.read_json} - src/core/handler/data/loader.py:21-26: {"csv": pd.read_csv, "excel": pd.read_excel, "json": pd.read_json, "classmethod": self.method}

Format Pydantic Validates? registry.py Handles? DataLoader Reads? Outcome csv ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Works json ❌ Rejected ✅ Yes ✅ Yes Schema validation blocks valid reader parquet ✅ Accepted ❌ No ❌ No Passes validation, crashes at runtime xlsx ✅ Accepted ❌ No ❌ No Passes validation, crashes at runtime

docs.title: 1. Total Absence of Automated Tests
docs.text: There is no tests/ directory anywhere in the project. The codebase has 0% automated test coverage. - No unit tests for transformers (MissingValueTransformer, ScalingTransformer, EncodingTransformer). - No tests for YAML schema validation, failure modes, or bad configurations. - No integration tests for Orchestrator execution. - Neither pytest nor any test runner is specified in dependencies.

docs.title: 2. Silent Error Masking in Context Managers
docs.text: In src/orchestrator.py:162-171: When an exception occurs during build() (such as a database connection failure), self.mlflow_tracker.run was previously uninitialized, causing AttributeError inside __exit__ and masking the true root cause with a secondary teardown exception.

docs.title: 1. Redundant In-Memory Data Duplication (src/core/handler/data/loader.py:71-76)
docs.text:
DataLoader loads raw tabular data into self.data, and immediately produces feature matrix self.X by dropping the target column: 

self.data = func(path)
self.X = self.data.drop(self.context.dataset.train.target_column, axis=1)
self.y = self.data[self.context.dataset.train.target_column]
DataFrame.drop(axis=1) creates a full copy of the feature matrix in memory. When self.data_splitter.split() executes, four additional DataFrames (x_train, x_test, y_train, y_test) are created. For large tabular datasets (e.g., millions of rows), this causes a 3x to 5x memory amplification, triggering Out-Of-Memory (OOM) faults.

docs.title: 2. State-Sharing in Pre-Instantiated Transformers (src/core/pipelines/transformers.py:139-143, 203-208)
docs.text:
ScalingTransformer and EncodingTransformer instantiate Scikit-Learn transformers inside __init__ in dictionaries: 

self._strategy_map = {
    "standard": StandardScaler(),
    "minmax": MinMaxScaler(),
    "robust": RobustScaler(),
}
If fit() is called repeatedly on different splits or pipelines, fitted state (e.g., mean_, scale_) lingers across invocations, introducing subtle state pollution risks.

docs.title: 1. Insecure Docker Compose Defaults
docs.text: In compose.yaml:93-98 and .env: - Default credentials are hardcoded in .env (POSTGRES_PASSWORD=mlflowpass, MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD=minioadminpass). - mlflow service runs as root inside the container. - Network configuration references an external unauthenticated network shared-infra-net: external: true.

docs.title: 2. Missing File Encoding in Configuration Loader (src/core/handler/config/loader.py:5)
docs.text:
with open(config_path, "r") as f:
    config = yaml.safe_load(f)
On Windows platforms, open() without an explicit encoding="utf-8" relies on the system default ANSI code page (e.g., cp1252), leading to UnicodeDecodeError when configuration files contain UTF-8 characters (accents, symbols, non-ASCII descriptions).

docs.title: CORR-001: Critical Evaluation Defect - Holdout Test Set Overwritten with Training Set
docs.text:
• Category: Correctness
  • Severity: Critical
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: src/orchestrator.py:73-78
  • Evidence: 
    x_train, x_test, y_train, y_test = self.data_splitter.split(
    X=self.data_loader.X,
    y=self.data_loader.y,
)
self.data_loader.X, self.data_loader.y = x_train, y_train
self.data_loader.X_test, self.data_loader.y_test = x_train, y_train
  • Problem: On line 78, x_train, y_train is assigned to X_test, y_test instead of x_test, y_test.
  • Impact: The pipeline evaluates holdout performance strictly on training data. Model metrics displayed in console logs and stored in artifacts reflect training accuracy, entirely masking overfitting and data leakage.
  • Recommended Direction: Correct line 78 to: self.data_loader.X_test, self.data_loader.y_test = x_test, y_test
  • Effort: Small
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: CORR-002: User-Configured random_state Completely Ignored
docs.text:
• Category: Correctness
  • Severity: High
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: src/core/handler/data/splitter.py:12
  • Evidence: 
    self.random_state = 42 or context.dataset.random_state
  • Problem: Because 42 is truthy in Python, 42 or <expr> unconditionally evaluates to 42.
  • Impact: The user's random_state setting in YAML is dead code; the split is permanently frozen at seed 42 regardless of configuration.
  • Recommended Direction: Reverse the operand order: self.random_state = context.dataset.random_state if context.dataset.random_state is not None else 42
  • Effort: Small
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: ARCH-001: Preprocessing Policies Crash on cleaning and filter Types
docs.text:
• Category: Architecture
  • Severity: Critical
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: src/core/context/contexts.py:85-87 & src/core/constants/registry.py:52-53
  • Evidence: 
    # contexts.py
policy_class = self.type.policy_class
if policy_class is None:
    raise ValueError(f"Unsupported preprocessing type: {self.type}")
self.params = policy_class(**self.params)

# registry.py
PreprocessingRegistry.cleaning: None,
PreprocessingRegistry.filter: None,
  • Problem: RunContext validates all preprocessing steps during model validation. For cleaning and filter, policy_class returns None, throwing ValueError and preventing any pipeline with these steps from running.
  • Impact: Feature cleaning and row filtering cannot be used despite transformers existing in src/core/pipelines/transformers.py.
  • Recommended Direction: Define dedicated Pydantic policies (CleaningPolicy, FilterPolicy) in policies.py and register them in PreprocessingRegistry.policy_class.
  • Effort: Small
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: ARCH-002: Missing MLflow Observability Instrumentation
docs.text:
• Category: Architecture
  • Severity: High
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: src/orchestrator.py:112-160
  • Evidence: Orchestrator.train() and Orchestrator.test() call evaluate(), which calculates accuracy_score and f1_score and logs to console.info, but never calls self.mlflow_tracker.log_metrics(). Furthermore, self.mlflow_tracker.log_params(), self.mlflow_tracker.log_model(), and self.mlflow_tracker.end_run() are never invoked anywhere in Orchestrator.
  • Problem: The platform fails to log hyperparameters, metrics, and models to MLflow.
  • Impact: The core value proposition of the repository (automated MLflow tracking) is unrealized; runs cannot be monitored or compared in the MLflow UI.
  • Recommended Direction: Instrument Orchestrator.build() to call log_params(self.context.model.hyperparameters), evaluate() to call self.mlflow_tracker.log_metrics(metrics), train() to call self.mlflow_tracker.log_model(self.pipeline), and __exit__() to call self.mlflow_tracker.end_run().
  • Effort: Medium
  • Dependencies: CORR-001

docs.title: ARCH-003: Contradictory File Format Contracts Across System Layers
docs.text:
• Category: Architecture
  • Severity: High
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: src/core/constants/constants.py:3-8, src/core/constants/registry.py:28-32, src/core/handler/data/loader.py:21-26
  • Evidence: FILE_TYPES allows "csv", "parquet", "excel", "xlsx". registry.py supports "csv", "excel", "json". loader.py duplicates registry.py and adds "classmethod": self.method.
  • Problem: Type definition drift across validation, registry, and execution layers.
  • Impact: Confusing developer experience; JSON is rejected at validation, while Parquet passes validation and fails at runtime.
  • Recommended Direction: Consolidate FILE_TYPES into a single canonical source of truth in src/core/constants/registry.py and implement proper reader functions or remove unsupported extensions.
  • Effort: Small
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: SMELL-001: Category Order Ignored in EncodingTransformer
docs.text:
• Category: Code Smell
  • Severity: High
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: src/core/pipelines/transformers.py:215-234
  • Evidence: 
    orders.append(col_detail.order)
...
transformers.append((f"{strategy}_encoding", obj, cols))
    orders is populated in line 220, but obj is taken from self._strategy_map["ordinal"] = OrdinalEncoder().
  • Problem: col_detail.order is never passed to OrdinalEncoder(categories=...).
  • Impact: Ordinal hierarchies specified in YAML are silently discarded and sorted alphabetically.
  • Recommended Direction: Construct individual OrdinalEncoder(categories=[col_detail.order]) instances per column when order is provided.
  • Effort: Medium
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: SMELL-002: FilterTransformer Violates Scikit-Learn Pipeline Invariants
docs.text:
• Category: Code Smell
  • Severity: High
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: src/core/pipelines/transformers.py:109-124
  • Evidence: 
    class FilterTransformer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
    def transform(self, X):
        return X.query(self.condition)
  • Problem: In Scikit-Learn, standard Pipeline.fit(X, y) transforms X step-by-step while y remains untouched. Dropping rows inside transform(X) desynchronizes the sample count between X and y.
  • Impact: Calling fit(X, y) on a pipeline containing FilterTransformer crashes with ValueError: Found input variables with inconsistent numbers of samples.
  • Recommended Direction: Relocate row filtering outside the Scikit-Learn pipeline directly into DataLoader or DataSplitter before feature/target extraction.
  • Effort: Medium
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: SMELL-003: main.run() Bypasses Arguments and Accesses Global Variable
docs.text:
• Category: Code Smell
  • Severity: Medium
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: main.py:10-12, 37
  • Evidence: 
    def run(*args, **kwargs):
    context = RunContext.from_yaml_dict(config)


...
run(**config)
  • Problem: run() accesses the module global config instead of accepting arguments.
  • Impact: Un-testable entry point; breaks Python import conventions.
  • Recommended Direction: Change signature to def run(config: dict): context = RunContext.from_yaml_dict(config).
  • Effort: Small
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: SMELL-004: Fragile Logging Handler Index Dependency
docs.text:

docs.title: SMELL-006: Uncontrolled File Creation on Module Import
docs.text:
• Category: Code Smell

docs.title: DEAD-001: Orphaned Prototype Files and Commented Blocks
docs.text:
• Category: Code Smell
  • Severity: Low
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: Multiple files (src/core/pipelines/temp_column_transformer.py, temp_feature_engineering.md, pipeline.py, features.py, src/core/models/linear.py, src/utils/data_loader.py, src/core/trackers/mlflow_tracker.py:63-160)
  • Evidence: Multiple empty or duplicate files and ~100 lines of commented code in production modules.
  • Problem: Accumulation of technical debt and uncurated scratch artifacts.
  • Impact: Increases cognitive overhead and confusion for developers and AI agents.
  • Recommended Direction: Delete orphaned files and remove commented-out dead code.
  • Effort: Small
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: TEST-001: Complete Absence of Automated Test Suite
docs.text:
• Category: Testing
  • Severity: Critical
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: Entire repository
  • Evidence: No tests/ directory exists. No test runner is configured.
  • Problem: Zero regression protection.
  • Impact: Critical defects (CORR-001, CORR-002, ARCH-001) went undetected.
  • Recommended Direction: Set up pytest in pyproject.toml, establish a tests/ directory with fixtures for YAML parsing, transformer behavior, and pipeline fitting.
  • Effort: Medium
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: PERF-001: Memory Amplification via Redundant Full DataFrame Copies
docs.text:
• Category: Performance
  • Severity: Medium
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: src/core/handler/data/loader.py:71-76, 93-98
  • Evidence: self.data = func(path), followed by self.X = self.data.drop(...) and self.y = self.data[...].
  • Problem: Retains both the full raw DataFrame and the feature/target splits simultaneously in memory.
  • Impact: High memory footprint on large datasets, leading to potential OOM failures.
  • Recommended Direction: Delete or overwrite self.data once X and y are extracted, or avoid duplicating column series.
  • Effort: Small
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: SEC-001: Hardcoded Credentials and External Network Assumptions in Docker Compose
docs.text:
• Category: Security
  • Severity: Low
  • Confidence: High
  • Location: compose.yaml:93-98 and .env
  • Evidence: Static default passwords in .env and external Docker network declarations (shared-infra-net: external: true).
  • Problem: Running docker compose up fails if external network is missing; default passwords pose risk if exposed.
  • Impact: Deployment friction and security risks in shared hosting environments.
  • Recommended Direction: Make shared-infra-net optional or create it in compose, and provide a .env.example template.
  • Effort: Small
  • Dependencies: None

docs.title: Quick Wins vs. Broader Refactoring
docs.text:
• Quick Wins (< 1 hour): CORR-001 (1-line fix), CORR-002 (1-line fix), ARCH-001 (add 2 Pydantic models), SMELL-005 (fix class syntax), SMELL-003 (add function parameter).
  • Broader Refactorings: TEST-001 (building comprehensive test harness), SMELL-002 (relocating filtering before pipeline building), ARCH-002 (full MLflow lifecycle integration).

docs.title: Areas That Should NOT Be Refactored Prematurely
docs.text:
• Pydantic Validation Layer: The Pydantic schema in src/core/context/ is well-designed. Do not discard it; simply fix the missing policy classes.
  • Scikit-Learn Pandas Integration: set_config(transform_output="pandas") is a major strength of this project. Do not replace it with custom array wrappers.

docs.title: 13. Positive Design Decisions and Existing Strengths
docs.text:
1. Strict Pandas DataFrame Output: Enforcing set_config(transform_output="pandas") across all Scikit-Learn transformers ensures feature names and column metadata are preserved throughout the transformation lifecycle.
  2. Pydantic Configuration Validation: Validating YAML configuration upfront before executing expensive data operations prevents late-stage pipeline crashes due to typos or invalid parameters.
  3. Decoupled Architecture: The separation between Data Loading, Data Splitting, Preprocessing Assembly, Model Building, and Tracking provides a modular foundation that can easily support new algorithms and preprocessing techniques once existing bugs are resolved.
  4. Modern Packaging with uv: Adopting uv and uv.lock enables fast, reproducible virtual environment provisioning and deterministic builds.
  5. Comprehensive Technical Documentation: The documentation site (built with Material for MkDocs) features thorough guides, architectural blueprints, and how-to recipes.

docs.title: 14. Audit Limitations and Unverified Hypotheses
docs.text:
• Multi-Node & Distributed Execution: The audit was conducted in a local single-node environment. Performance behavior under distributed workloads (e.g., Dask, Spark) was not evaluated.
  • Large Dataset Profiling (PERF-001): Memory amplification was identified through static code inspection of Pandas transformations; empirical memory profiling with memory-profiler on multi-gigabyte datasets should be conducted to measure exact heap usage.
  • External Docker Infrastructure: The Docker Compose stack relies on an external network (shared-infra-net) that was not running during the audit; live PostgreSQL/MinIO integration could not be verified against the Docker compose definition.

docs.title: Execution Flow
docs.text:
This document walks you step-by-step through what happens under the hood when you run:

uv run python -m main --config configs/mvp.yaml

docs.title: Step-by-Step Sequence
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User
    participant CLI as main.py
    participant Loader as config_loader
    participant Context as RunContext (Pydantic)
    participant Orch as Orchestrator
    participant MLflow as MLflowTracker
    participant Data as DataLoader & DataSplitter
    participant Pipeline as Scikit-Learn Pipeline

    User->>CLI: Run python -m main --config configs/mvp.yaml
    CLI->>Loader: Read and parse YAML file
    Loader-->>CLI: Return raw config dict
    CLI->>Context: RunContext.from_yaml_dict(config)
    Note over Context: Validate data types & cast step policies
    Context-->>CLI: Return strongly-typed RunContext
    CLI->>Orch: Start Orchestrator context manager

    Orch->>MLflow: start_run()
    Note over MLflow: Create/set experiment & open active run

    Orch->>Data: load_data() & split(X, y)
    Note over Data: Partition into train & test splits
    Data-->>Orch: Return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test

    Orch->>Pipeline: Assemble Pipeline(preprocessing_steps + model_step)

    Orch->>Pipeline: fit(X_train, y_train)
    Note over Pipeline: Transformers calculate means, medians, categories
    Note over Pipeline: Model learns coefficients/trees

    Orch->>Pipeline: predict(X_test)
    Note over Pipeline: Transformers apply learned rules to test set
    Pipeline-->>Orch: Return y_pred

    Orch->>Orch: evaluate(y_test, y_pred)
    Note over Orch: Calculate Accuracy & F1 score

    Orch->>MLflow: Upload session log artifact on exit
    MLflow-->>User: Run finished & logged to MLflow UI

docs.title: Why Splitting First Matters (Preventing Data Leakage)
docs.text:
Data Leakage is one of the most common and costly mistakes in machine learning. It happens when information from your test set accidentally leaks into the training process.

For example: - If you compute the mean of a column across the entire dataset before splitting, the training data now has knowledge of the test set's distribution. - If you fit a MinMaxScaler on all rows, the minimum and maximum values will include test rows.

In mlflow-experience, data leakage is impossible by design: 1. The split happens first: DataLoader loads the data, and DataSplitter immediately splits it into training and testing sets. 2. Transformers only see the training set: When pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train) is called, Scikit-Learn only computes statistics (like means, standard deviations, or category mappings) on $X_{train}$. 3. The test set is transformed blindly: When pipeline.predict(X_test) runs, Scikit-Learn calls .transform() on each step, applying the rules learned during training without recalculating anything.

docs.title: The Orchestrator Engine
docs.text: The Orchestrator class (src/orchestrator.py) is the main coordinator of the whole pipeline.

docs.title: How It Is Used
docs.text:
In main.py, the Orchestrator is executed as a Python context manager:

from src.core.context.contexts import RunContext
from src.orchestrator import Orchestrator

# 1. Parse and validate the YAML dictionary into a RunContext
context = RunContext.from_yaml_dict(config)

# 2. Run the pipeline inside the context manager
with Orchestrator(context) as orchestrator:
    orchestrator.build()
    orchestrator.train()
    orchestrator.test()

Using with Orchestrator(...) as orchestrator: ensures that when the run finishes—or even if an unhandled exception crashes the program—the __exit__ block runs and uploads the session log to MLflow!

docs.title: The Lifecycle Stages
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Initialized: __init__(RunContext)
    Initialized --> Running: __enter__()
    Running --> PipelineBuilt: build()
    PipelineBuilt --> ModelTrained: train()
    ModelTrained --> ModelEvaluated: test()
    ModelEvaluated --> LogsPersisted: __exit__()
    LogsPersisted --> [*]

docs.title: 1. Initialization (__init__)
docs.text: When created, the Orchestrator initializes its constituent builders and trackers: - self.data_loader: Prepares data loading logic. - self.data_splitter: Prepares data splitting logic. - self.preprocessor: Prepares the preprocessing transformer factory. - self.model_builder: Prepares the model estimator factory. - self.mlflow_tracker: Connects to the MLflow tracking server.

docs.title: 2. Build Stage (orchestrator.build())
docs.text: This method puts the pieces together: 1. Calls self.mlflow_tracker.start_run() to start a new experiment run in MLflow. 2. Calls self.data_loader.load_data() to read the data from disk. 3. If no separate test file was provided in the YAML, calls self.data_splitter.split(X, y) to partition the data into training and testing sets. 4. Calls self.preprocessor.build() to get a list of Scikit-Learn transformer tuples [(name, transformer), ...]. 5. Calls self.model_builder.build() to get the estimator tuple [(task_name, model)]. 6. Combines the transformer steps and model step into self.pipeline = Pipeline(self.pipeline_steps).

docs.title: 3. Training Stage (orchestrator.train())
docs.text:
Fits the compiled pipeline: 

self.pipeline = self.pipeline.fit(self.data_loader.X, self.data_loader.y)
Then predicts on the training data and calls self.evaluate() to log in-sample performance metrics.

docs.title: 4. Testing Stage (orchestrator.test())
docs.text:
Evaluates the model on unseen test data: 

y_pred = self.pipeline.predict(self.data_loader.X_test)
self.evaluate(y_true=self.data_loader.y_test, y_pred=y_pred)

docs.title: 5. Prediction Stage (orchestrator.predict(X))
docs.text:
Passes new observations $X$ through the fitted pipeline: 

def predict(self, X):
    return self.pipeline.predict(X)
The data is automatically cleaned, scaled, and encoded using the exact parameters learned during training, and final predictions are returned.

docs.title: 6. Exit & Cleanup Stage (__exit__)
docs.text:
When exiting the context manager: 1. The active session log file is identified from the logger handlers. 2. The log file is uploaded as an artifact to MLflow: 

self.mlflow_tracker.log_artifact(
    console.handlers[1].baseFilename,
    f"logs/{self.mlflow_tracker.run.info.run_name}.log",
)
This guarantees you can always trace back any MLflow run to its exact execution log.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: This section explains the design behind mlflow-experience so you understand how all the parts fit together.

docs.title: The Core Idea: Clean Separation of Concerns
docs.text:
In a typical data science project, data loading, cleaning, scaling, feature engineering, modeling, and logging are often mixed together inside a single script or notebook.

mlflow-experience separates these tasks into 5 distinct layers:

graph TD
    Layer5["5. Orchestrator (Coordinates the Run)"]
    Layer4["4. Pipelines & Transformers (Cleans Data & Trains Model)"]
    Layer3["3. Data Handlers (Loads & Splits Data)"]
    Layer2["2. Configuration (Validates YAML Settings)"]
    Layer1["1. Observability (Logs Events & MLflow Artifacts)"]

    Layer5 --> Layer4
    Layer5 --> Layer3
    Layer5 --> Layer2
    Layer5 --> Layer1

docs.title: Layer 1: Infrastructure & Observability (The Foundation)
docs.text:
• Files: src/core/trackers/mlflow_tracker.py, src/core/logging/logger.py
  • What it does: Handles logging and tracking. It connects to MLflow (locally or via Docker), logs your parameters, scores, and models, and writes timestamped logs to src/core/logs/.

docs.title: Layer 2: Configuration & Validation (The Brain)
docs.text:
• Files: src/core/handler/config/loader.py, src/core/context/contexts.py, src/core/context/policies.py
  • What it does: Reads your YAML file and validates it using Pydantic v2. If you have a typo in a strategy name (e.g. stragegy: meann), it throws an error immediately before any heavy data loading or model fitting starts.

docs.title: Layer 3: Data Management (The I/O Layer)
docs.text:
• Files: src/core/handler/data/loader.py, src/core/handler/data/splitter.py
  • What it does: Loads your raw files (CSV, Excel, JSON) into Pandas DataFrames. It finds the file path automatically, separates the target column $y$ from features $X$, and performs train/test splitting.

docs.title: Layer 4: Transformation & ML Logic (The Engine)
docs.text:
• Files: src/core/pipelines/preprocessing.py, src/core/pipelines/transformers.py, src/core/pipelines/model_builder.py
  • What it does: Creates Scikit-Learn transformers (imputers, scalers, encoders) from your configuration and wraps them into a single sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline with the final model estimator.

docs.title: Layer 5: Orchestration (The Conductor)
docs.text:
• Files: src/orchestrator.py
  • What it does: Coordinates the entire sequence from start to finish. It manages the lifecycle using Python's context manager (with Orchestrator(context) as orch:), guaranteeing that execution logs are safely stored even if an error occurs.

docs.title: Why Use Scikit-Learn Pipelines?
docs.text: By combining all preprocessing and the model into one sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline object: 1. Preventing Data Leakage: Transformers only learn statistics (like column means or category frequencies) during .fit() on the training split. During .predict(), they apply those learned statistics without peeking at the test set. 2. Atomic Serialization: The entire preprocessing pipeline and trained model can be saved and deployed together as a single artifact in MLflow. 3. Reproducibility: Any future data fed into pipeline.predict(X_new) will automatically undergo the exact same cleaning, encoding, and scaling steps.

docs.title: Configuration Examples
docs.text: Below are complete, production-ready configuration examples included with the repository.

docs.title: 1. Logistic Regression Baseline (configs/mvp.yaml)
docs.text:
This configuration runs a linear classifier on telecom churn data, including renaming, missing value imputation, ordinal/one-hot encoding, and scaling.

project:
  name: customer_churn_prediction
  owner: data_science_team
  environment: production
  description: Predict customer churn for telecom users

mlflow:
  experiment_name: customer_churn_experiments
  experiment_id: NA
  track_params: true
  track_metrics: true
  track_artifacts:
    - feature_config
    - preprocessing_objects
    - model
  tags:
    project: churn
    stage: production
    owner: data_science_team

dataset:
  dataset_name: telecom_churn_v1
  random_state: 52
  train_test_split: 0.2
  train:
    type: csv
    path: data/raw/churn_train.csv
    id_column: CustomerID
    target_column: Churn
    positive_class: 1

preprocessing:
  - name: rename_columns
    type: rename
    params:
      mapping:
        CustomerID: customer_id
        Usage Frequency: usage_frequency
        Support Calls: support_calls
        Payment Delay: payment_delay
        Subscription Type: subscription_type
        Contract Length: contract_length
        Total Spend: total_spend
        Last Interaction: last_interaction

  - name: cast_types
    type: type_cast
    params:
      columns:
        - name: Age
          dtype: int
        - name: Gender
          dtype: str
        - name: Tenure
          dtype: int

  - name: handle_missing
    type: missing
    params:
      columns:
        - name: Age
          strategy: mean
        - name: Gender
          strategy: mode

  - name: encode_features
    type: encoding
    params:
      columns:
        - name: Gender
          strategy: ordinal
          order: ['Male', 'Female']
        - name: contract_length
          strategy: ordinal
          order: ['Monthly', 'Quarterly', 'Annual']
        - name: subscription_type
          strategy: one_hot

  - name: scale_features
    type: scaling
    params:
      columns:
        - name: Age
          strategy: standard
        - name: total_spend
          strategy: minmax

model:
  type: logistic_regression
  task: 'binary:classification'
  hyperparameters:
    C: 1.0
    max_iter: 250
    solver: saga

training:
  objective: binary:logistic

evaluation:
  metrics:
    - accuracy
    - f1

docs.title: Pydantic Policies & Validation
docs.text: To make development reliable and prevent silent runtime crashes, mlflow-experience validates all configuration settings using Pydantic v2 (src/core/context/contexts.py and src/core/context/policies.py).

docs.title: Why Use Pydantic?
docs.text:
In traditional ML projects with YAML files, a simple typo (such as strategy: meaan or omitting a required column) would only fail deep inside Scikit-Learn code after 10 minutes of execution.

With Pydantic: - Instant Failure: Your configuration is checked before any data is loaded or processed. - Helpful Error Messages: It tells you the exact line, field name, and expected values if something is wrong. - Automatic Type Conversion: String numbers are parsed into integers or floats automatically where appropriate.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When main.py runs, it calls:

context = RunContext.from_yaml_dict(config)
  1. Pydantic parses the dictionary against RunContext.
  2. A model validator (cast_all_preprocessing_params) checks each step in preprocessing.
  3. The step's type looks up the corresponding policy class from PreprocessingRegistry.policy_class.
  4. The dictionary is instantiated into a strongly-typed policy object (e.g. MissingValuePolicy, ScalingPolicy, EncodingPolicy).

docs.title: RenamePolicy
docs.text: Validates column rename mappings: - mapping (dict[str, str]): Must not be empty.

docs.title: MissingValuePolicy
docs.text: Validates missing value strategies: - strategy: Must be one of "mean", "median", "mode", or "constant". - fill_value: Required if strategy: constant.

docs.title: EncodingPolicy
docs.text: Validates encoding configurations: - strategy: Must be one of "one_hot", "ordinal", "label", or "target". - order: A list of strings specifying the exact order for ordinal encoding (e.g. ['Low', 'Medium', 'High']).

docs.title: ScalingPolicy
docs.text: Validates scaling strategies: - strategy: Must be one of "standard", "minmax", or "robust".

docs.title: Example Error Output
docs.text:
If you provide an invalid strategy in your YAML:

- name: bad_step
  type: missing
  params:
    columns:
      - name: age
        strategy: invalid_strategy

Pydantic immediately catches it:

pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for MissingValueConfig
strategy
  Input should be 'mean', 'median', 'mode' or 'constant' [type=literal_error, input_value='invalid_strategy', input_type=str]

docs.title: YAML Configuration Reference
docs.text: This guide is the complete reference for every section and option you can put in your experiment YAML file.

docs.title: Structure Overview
docs.text:
Every configuration file has 7 top-level sections:

project:       # Who owns this experiment and what environment is it for?
mlflow:        # Where should MLflow log the run and what should it track?
dataset:       # What data are we training on, and how should it be split?
preprocessing: # What cleaning, imputation, encoding, and scaling steps are needed?
model:         # Which machine learning model should we train?
training:      # What is the training objective?
evaluation:    # Which evaluation metrics should be reported?

docs.title: 1. project
docs.text:
Defines basic metadata for organizational tracking.

project:
  name: customer_churn_prediction  # Project identifier (string)
  owner: data_science_team          # Team or author name (string)
  environment: production           # "development", "staging", or "production"
  description: Telecom churn model  # Optional human description (string)

docs.title: 2. mlflow
docs.text:
Controls where experiment results, metrics, parameters, and models are sent.

mlflow:
  experiment_name: customer_churn_experiments  # MLflow experiment name (created if missing)
  tracking_uri: http://localhost:5000         # MLflow server URL (default: http://localhost:5000)
  track_params: true                          # Log hyperparameters and options (default: true)
  track_metrics: true                         # Log evaluation metrics (default: true)
  track_artifacts:                            # Optional list of artifact names to log
    - model
    - preprocessing_objects
  tags:                                       # Custom key-value tags for easy filtering in UI
    stage: production
    team: analytics

Running without Docker

If you are not running a Docker MLflow server on port 5000, you can set tracking_uri: sqlite:///mlflow.db or tracking_uri: file:./mlruns to track everything locally!

docs.title: 3. dataset
docs.text:
Specifies where to load the training (and optional test) data and how to handle targets and splitting.

dataset:
  dataset_name: telecom_churn_v1 # Dataset name label
  random_state: 42               # Seed for reproducible splitting (integer >= 0)
  train_test_split: 0.2          # Ratio to reserve for testing if no test dataset is given (e.g. 0.2 = 20%)

  # Training dataset source (Required)
  train:
    type: csv                    # "csv", "excel", "xlsx", or "json"
    path: data/raw/churn_train.csv # Path to the file (relative or absolute)
    id_column: CustomerID        # Unique identifier column (ignored during training)
    target_column: Churn         # Target variable column to predict

  # Dedicated test dataset source (Optional)
  test:
    type: csv
    path: data/raw/churn_test.csv
    id_column: CustomerID
    target_column: Churn

docs.title: 4. preprocessing
docs.text:
An ordered list of transformation steps. Steps execute in the exact order you write them.

Each step has: - name: A descriptive name for the step (e.g. handle_missing_age). - type: The transformer type matching PreprocessingRegistry. - params: The options for that transformer.

Here are the supported preprocessing types and their parameters:

docs.title: A. rename (Rename Columns)
docs.text:
Renames raw column headers (e.g. stripping spaces, standardizing to lowercase snake_case):

- name: rename_columns
  type: rename
  params:
    mapping:
      "Customer ID": customer_id
      "Total Spend": total_spend
      "Support Calls": support_calls

docs.title: B. type_cast (Cast Data Types)
docs.text:
Converts column data types:

- name: cast_types
  type: type_cast
  params:
    columns:
      - name: age
        dtype: int
      - name: gender
        dtype: str
      - name: tenure
        dtype: int

docs.title: C. missing (Impute Missing Values)
docs.text:
Handles missing values on a per-column basis:

- name: handle_missing
  type: missing
  params:
    columns:
      - name: age
        strategy: mean         # Options: mean, median, mode, constant

      - name: support_calls
        strategy: median

      - name: gender
        strategy: mode         # Uses the most frequent value

      - name: city
        strategy: constant     # Injects a custom fill value
        fill_value: "Unknown"

docs.title: D. encoding (Categorical Encoding)
docs.text:
Encodes categorical text columns into numbers:

- name: encode_features
  type: encoding
  params:
    columns:
      # Ordinal encoding: Maps values to integers using the exact order specified
      - name: contract_length
        strategy: ordinal
        order: ['Monthly', 'Quarterly', 'Annual']

      - name: gender
        strategy: ordinal
        order: ['Male', 'Female']

      # One-Hot encoding: Creates binary indicator columns for each category
      - name: subscription_type
        strategy: one_hot

docs.title: E. scaling (Numerical Feature Scaling)
docs.text:
Scales numeric features to standard ranges:

- name: scale_features
  type: scaling
  params:
    columns:
      # StandardScaler: Zero mean, unit variance
      - name: age
        strategy: standard

      # MinMaxScaler: Scaled to [0, 1] range
      - name: total_spend
        strategy: minmax

      # RobustScaler: Scaled using median and interquartile range (outlier-resilient)
      - name: payment_delay
        strategy: robust

docs.text:
Replaces specific values or fixes typos:

- name: clean_categories
  type: cleaning
  params:
    replacements:
      contract:
        "month-to-month": "Monthly"
        "12 Month": "Annual"

docs.title: G. filter (Row Filtering)
docs.text:
Filters rows based on a query condition:

- name: remove_invalid_tenure
  type: filter
  params:
    condition: "tenure >= 0 and total_spend >= 0"

docs.title: 5. model
docs.text:
Defines which model to train and its hyperparameters.

model:
  type: logistic_regression          # "logistic_regression" or "xgboost"
  task: 'binary:classification'      # Task identifier name
  hyperparameters:                   # Passed directly to the model constructor
    C: 1.0
    max_iter: 250
    solver: saga

For XGBoost:

model:
  type: xgboost
  task: 'xgboost:classification'
  hyperparameters:
    n_estimators: 500
    learning_rate: 0.01
    max_depth: 6
    random_state: 42

docs.title: 6. training & evaluation
docs.text:
Defines training objective flags and the metrics to calculate:

training:
  objective: binary:logistic

evaluation:
  metrics:
    - accuracy
    - f1

docs.title: 3. Extending the Codebase: Recipes for Agents
Recipe A: Adding a New Preprocessing Transformer
docs.text:
To add a new transformer (e.g. ClipOutliersTransformer):

  1. Implement the Transformer in src/core/pipelines/transformers.py:
  2. Inherit from BaseEstimator and TransformerMixin.
  3. Learn parameters strictly in fit(X, y). Never compute statistics in __init__ or transform.

  4. Apply transformations in transform(X). Ensure output is a DataFrame (X.copy()).

  5. Define Pydantic Policy in src/core/context/policies.py:

  6. Create a typed config (e.g. ClipOutliersPolicy(BaseModel)).

  7. Register the Step in src/core/constants/registry.py:

  8. Add enum member to PreprocessingRegistry: 
    clip_outliers = "clip_outliers"

  9. Map policy_class and transformer_class in their respective properties.

  10. Instantiate in src/core/pipelines/preprocessing.py:

  11. Ensure _instantiate_transformer() extracts the policy parameters and initializes the transformer instance.

docs.title: Recipe B: Adding a New Model Estimator
docs.text:
To add a new model (e.g. RandomForestClassifier or LightGBM):

  1. Update Enum & Mapping in src/core/constants/registry.py:
  2. Add to ModelType: 
    random_forest = "random_forest"

  3. In ModelType.model_class property: 

    ModelType.random_forest: RandomForestClassifier

  4. Instantiate in Model Builder (src/core/models/linear.py):

To support a new format (e.g. parquet):

  2. Register reader in DATA_READER_FUNCTIONS in src/core/constants/registry.py: 
    "parquet": pd.read_parquet,

docs.title: 4. Invariants & Rules You Must Never Break
docs.text:
[!IMPORTANT] 1. DataFrames Stay DataFrames: Never drop column names into a raw NumPy array during preprocessing unless explicitly requested. Always keep set_config(transform_output="pandas") active.

  1. Zero Data Leakage: Never compute global parameters across train and test sets combined. Imputers, scalers, and encoders must only fit on X_train.

  2. Dual Logging Discipline: Never use bare print() calls in src/. Always use: 

    from src.core.logging.logger import console
console.info("Descriptive log message")
console.debug("Low-level debugging info")
console.error("Failure reason")

  3. Sequential Execution Awareness: Preprocessing steps in YAML execute sequentially. If Step 1 renames column old_col → new_col, Step 2 (scaling/encoding) must refer to new_col.

  4. Pydantic Validation Guard: All configuration values must be validated by Pydantic before any data processing starts. Never access unvalidated raw dictionary keys directly inside pipelines.

  5. Path Resolution: Do not rely on os.getcwd() for relative file paths. Always use resolve_path() from src.utils.path_resolver.

docs.title: 5. Pre-Completion Verification Checklist
docs.text:
Before reporting any coding task as finished, run these verification steps in order:

  • Run Baseline Pipeline: 
    uv run python -m main --config configs/mvp.yaml
    (Must complete with exit code 0 and log metrics to MLflow).
  • Run XGBoost Pipeline: 
    uv run python -m main --config configs/mvp_xgboost.yaml
    (Must complete with exit code 0).
  • Verify Documentation: 
    uv run mkdocs build --strict
    (Must build in strict mode with 0 errors and 0 warnings).
  • Code Hygiene: Ensure no temporary debug files, scratch files, or unwanted .db files are left uncommitted or unignored.

docs.title: 6. Common Pitfalls & Solutions
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix KeyError: 'Age' in scaling step A prior rename step changed 'Age' to 'age'. Check pipeline order in YAML; use the renamed column name in subsequent steps. MLflow connection refused (localhost:5000) Docker MLflow server is not running. Set tracking_uri: sqlite:///mlflow.db in the YAML file for offline local tracking. Transformer returns NumPy array Transformer did not respect Scikit-Learn pandas output. Set set_config(transform_output="pandas") and return X.copy(). ValueError: Input contains NaN Scaler or encoder was placed before missing value imputer. Place missing imputer before scaling and encoding in the YAML list. Broken link in docs during build File was created but not registered in mkdocs.yml navigation. Add the path to nav in mkdocs.yml.

• Any new YAML configuration field must be validated through a Pydantic model in src/core/context/contexts.py or src/core/context/policies.py.

docs.title: Scikit-Learn Transformer Guidelines
docs.text: When authoring custom transformers in src/core/pipelines/transformers.py: 1. Inheritance: Always inherit from BaseEstimator and TransformerMixin. 2. State Learning: Learn all parameters (means, medians, scales, categories) only during fit(X, y=None). 3. docs.title: Example: Adding RandomForestClassifier
docs.text: Suppose you want to support Scikit-Learn's RandomForestClassifier.

docs.title: Step 1: Update ModelType (src/core/constants/registry.py)
docs.text:
1. Import the model class at the top of the file: 

    from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

  2. Add the enum value and map it in model_class: 

    class ModelType(str, Enum):
    logistic_regression = "logistic_regression"
    xgboost = "xgboost"
    random_forest = "random_forest"  # <--- Add this

    @property
    def model_class(self):
        mapping = {
            ModelType.logistic_regression: LogisticRegression,
            ModelType.xgboost: XGBClassifier,
            ModelType.random_forest: RandomForestClassifier,  # <--- Add this
        }
        return mapping.get(self)

docs.title: Step 2: Use It in Your YAML Configuration
docs.text:
You can now use random_forest in any configuration file. Any parameters you pass under hyperparameters will be forwarded directly to the RandomForestClassifier constructor:

model:
  type: random_forest
  task: 'random_forest:classification'
  hyperparameters:
    n_estimators: 200
    max_depth: 10
    min_samples_split: 5
    random_state: 42
    n_jobs: -1

docs.title: Step 3: Run the Pipeline
docs.text:
uv run python -m main --config configs/your_config.yaml

The ModelBuilder will automatically instantiate RandomForestClassifier with your hyperparameters and add it as the final step of the pipeline.

docs.title: Adding a New Transformer
docs.text: This tutorial shows you how to add a new preprocessing transformer to mlflow-experience in 4 simple steps.

docs.title: Example: Building an Outlier Clipping Transformer
docs.text: Let's say you want to build an OutlierTransformer that clips values above or below specific quantiles.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the Policy (src/core/context/policies.py)
docs.text:
Define the Pydantic models to validate the YAML settings:

# src/core/context/policies.py


class OutlierConfig(ColumnConfig):
    method: Literal["clip", "zscore"] = "clip"
    lower_quantile: Optional[float] = 0.01
    upper_quantile: Optional[float] = 0.99


class OutlierPolicy(BaseModel):
    columns: List[OutlierConfig]

docs.title: Step 2: Implement the Transformer (src/core/pipelines/transformers.py)
docs.text:
Create a class that inherits from BaseEstimator and TransformerMixin:

# src/core/pipelines/transformers.py
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin


class OutlierTransformer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
    def __init__(self, params=None):
        self.params = params
        self.bounds_ = {}

    def fit(self, X, y=None):
        # Learn upper and lower bounds on training set ONLY
        if hasattr(self.params, "columns"):
            for col in self.params.columns:
                lower = X[col.name].quantile(col.lower_quantile)
                upper = X[col.name].quantile(col.upper_quantile)
                self.bounds_[col.name] = (lower, upper)
        return self

    def transform(self, X):
        X = X.copy()
        for col_name, (lower, upper) in self.bounds_.items():
            if col_name in X.columns:
                X[col_name] = X[col_name].clip(lower=lower, upper=upper)
        return X

docs.title: Step 3: Register in PreprocessingRegistry (src/core/constants/registry.py)
docs.text:
Add your new type to PreprocessingRegistry:

# src/core/constants/registry.py


class PreprocessingRegistry(str, Enum):
    # ... existing entries ...
    outliers = "outliers"

    @property
    def policy_class(self):
        mapping = {
            # ... existing mappings ...
            PreprocessingRegistry.outliers: OutlierPolicy,
        }
        return mapping.get(self)

    @property
    def transformer_class(self):
        mapping = {
            # ... existing mappings ...
            PreprocessingRegistry.outliers: OutlierTransformer,
        }
        return mapping.get(self)

docs.title: Step 4: Use It in Your YAML File
docs.text:
Add the step to preprocessing in your config:

preprocessing:
  - name: clip_outliers
    type: outliers
    params:
      columns:
        - name: total_spend
          method: clip
          lower_quantile: 0.01
          upper_quantile: 0.99

Run the pipeline:

uv run python -m main --config configs/mvp.yaml

Your new transformer will be instantiated, fitted on training data, applied to test data, and included in the pipeline!

docs.title: Future Enhancements & Architectural Scenarios
docs.text: This document outlines the strategic roadmap, planned architectural evolutions, and feature scenarios for mlflow-experience. It bridges the initial prototype and MVP tasks into an enterprise-ready, declarative MLOps platform.

docs.title: 🎯 Vision Statement
docs.text: mlflow-experience aims to be the most intuitive declarative MLOps framework: - Developers and data scientists describe what they want (data, cleaning, transformations, models, metrics) in structured YAML. - The engine handles how it executes (leakage-free splitting, dependency resolution, execution telemetry, model tracking, and production export). - Autonomous AI agents can navigate the configuration space to iterate on experiments without human intervention.

docs.title: 📊 Future Capabilities Matrix
docs.text: Scenario Focus Area Impact Complexity Target Layer 1. Autonomous Auto-Config AI Agent LLM Automation 🔥 High Medium Orchestration / CLI 2. DAG Pipeline & Branching Engine Preprocessing 🔥 High High Preprocessing Engine 3. Cloud Lakehouse & DuckDB Ingestion Data Ingestion Medium Medium Data Ingestion Layer 4. Declarative Hyperparameter Tuning (HPO) Model Training 🔥 High Medium Training Engine 5. Production Serving & ONNX Export Deployment 🔥 High High Serving Layer 6. Data Drift & Automated Retraining Monitoring Medium Medium Observability 7. MLflow Tracing & Step Telemetry Observability Medium Low Tracking Engine 8. Visual Web Pipeline Builder UI Developer UX Medium High UI / Tooling

docs.title: Problem Statement
docs.text: Currently, humans must inspect data distributions manually, choose imputation strategies, identify high-cardinality features, write YAML files, and run commands.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text:
Introduce an AI agent mode via uv run python -m agent that: 1. Profiles a raw dataset (column types, null ratios, cardinality, skewness). 2. Generates multiple candidate YAML configuration strategies: - Baseline linear model with standard scaling. - Robust tree model with target/ordinal encoding. - Complex model with interaction features. 3. Automatically launches concurrent experiments, analyzes MLflow metrics, and returns a markdown comparison report with the winning run.

graph TD
    Data[Raw Data File] --> Profiler[Dataset Profiler]
    Profiler --> LLM[Auto-Config Agent]
    LLM --> ConfigA["Config A: Logistic (Baseline)"]
    LLM --> ConfigB["Config B: XGBoost (Robust)"]
    LLM --> ConfigC["Config C: LightGBM (Tuned)"]
    ConfigA --> Runner[Orchestrator Engine]
    ConfigB --> Runner
    ConfigC --> Runner
    Runner --> MLflow[(MLflow Tracking)]
    MLflow --> DecisionEngine[Decision Briefing]
    DecisionEngine --> Winner[Deployable Winner Model]

docs.title: Proposed CLI Interface
docs.text:
uv run python -m agent \
  --data data/raw/customer_churn.csv \
  --target Churn \
  --goal "Maximize F1 score while prioritizing model interpretability" \
  --max-trials 5

docs.title: Scenario 2: DAG Pipeline and Branching Engine
Problem Statement
docs.text: The current preprocessing engine is strictly linear: $$\text{Step 1} \to \text{Step 2} \to \text{Step 3}$$ Real-world pipelines require branching and multi-modal handling: - Numeric features need median imputation followed by robust scaling. - Text features need tokenization and TF-IDF / vector embeddings. - Categorical features need target encoding or one-hot encoding. - All branches must be combined prior to estimator training.

docs.title: Proposed Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    Raw[Raw Ingestion] --> Split[Train/Test Split]
    Split --> Impute[Global Imputation]

    Impute --> BranchNum[Numeric Branch]
    Impute --> BranchCat[Categorical Branch]
    Impute --> BranchText[Text NLP Branch]

    BranchNum --> Scaling[RobustScaler]
    BranchCat --> Encoding[TargetEncoder]
    BranchText --> Embeddings[TF-IDF / Vectorizer]

    Scaling --> Merge[Feature Union / Junction]
    Encoding --> Merge
    Embeddings --> Merge

    Merge --> Estimator[Model Estimator]

docs.title: Proposed YAML Schema
docs.text:
preprocessing:
  execution_mode: dag # "linear" | "dag"
  nodes:
    - id: impute_step
      type: missing
      params: { ... }

    - id: scale_numerics
      type: scaling
      depends_on: [impute_step]
      params: { ... }

    - id: encode_categoricals
      type: encoding
      depends_on: [impute_step]
      params: { ... }

    - id: merge_features
      type: feature_union
      depends_on: [scale_numerics, encode_categoricals]

docs.title: Scenario 3: Cloud Storage, Lakehouse, and Modern Formats
Problem Statement
docs.text: Production datasets reside in cloud buckets (AWS S3, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage) and columnar lakehouses, not local CSV files. Loading 50GB CSV files into Pandas causes Out-Of-Memory (OOM) crashes.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text:
1. Cloud Connectors: Direct streaming/download from s3://, gs://, and abfss://.
  2. Columnar Ingestion: Native support for Apache Parquet and Apache Arrow with lazy schema evaluation.
  3. DuckDB In-Memory SQL Ingestion: Filter and aggregate multi-gigabyte files before loading into memory.

docs.title: Proposed YAML Schema
docs.text:
dataset:
  dataset_name: enterprise_churn_v2
  train:
    type: parquet
    path: s3://mlops-prod-data/telecom/churn_2026_q1.parquet
    storage_options:
      key: env:AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
      secret: env:AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    sql_query: >
      SELECT customer_id, age, tenure, monthly_charges, churn
      FROM read_parquet('s3://...')
      WHERE status = 'ACTIVE' AND age >= 18
    id_column: customer_id
    target_column: churn

docs.title: Scenario 4: Declarative Hyperparameter Tuning with Optuna
Problem Statement
docs.text: Currently, users must manually edit YAML hyperparameters for each experiment run.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text: Integrate Optuna to perform Bayesian Optimization (Tree-structured Parzen Estimator) directly driven by YAML:

docs.title: Proposed YAML Schema
docs.text:
tuning:
  enabled: true
  framework: optuna
  n_trials: 50
  timeout_seconds: 1800
  metric: f1
  direction: maximize

  search_space:
    model.hyperparameters.learning_rate:
      type: float
      low: 0.001
      high: 0.3
      log: true
    model.hyperparameters.max_depth:
      type: int
      low: 3
      high: 12
    model.hyperparameters.n_estimators:
      type: categorical
      choices: [100, 200, 500]

docs.title: MLflow Integration
docs.text: Each Optuna trial automatically logs as a nested child run inside MLflow with parameter coordinates, trial duration, and optimization history contour plots.

docs.title: Scenario 5: Production Serving and Export Engine
Problem Statement
docs.text: After training a winning model, deploying it into an operational service requires manual packaging and glue code.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text: Add an automated export and serving CLI to turn any trained run into a high-throughput microservice.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:

docs.title: Scenario 6: Data Drift and Continuous Monitoring
Problem Statement
docs.text: Models degrade silently over time as real-world distributions shift away from baseline training distributions.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text:
Integrate Evidently AI or Great Expectations directly into the evaluation layer: 1. Data Drift Detection: Compare production scoring batches against the training baseline using Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) tests and Population Stability Index (PSI). 2. Concept Drift: Track rolling precision/recall when ground-truth labels arrive. 3. Automated Alerting: Push drift reports directly into MLflow Artifacts and trigger webhook alerts when drift score exceeds predefined thresholds.

monitoring:
  drift_detection:
    enabled: true
    confidence_level: 0.95
    alert_threshold_psi: 0.25
    report_format: html

docs.title: Scenario 7: MLflow Tracing and Step-Level Telemetry
Problem Statement
docs.text: Currently, MLflow logs pipeline-level summary metrics (accuracy, F1, latency), but gives no visibility into which individual transformer is slow or causing memory spikes.

docs.title: Proposed Solution
docs.text:
Adopt MLflow Tracing and a @track_step execution wrapper: - Log execution duration per step in milliseconds. - Log memory delta (RAM before vs after transformation). - Log feature dimensional changes (e.g., input: 12 features → output: 34 features after one-hot encoding). - Generate a waterfall visualization in the MLflow UI.

[Pipeline Execution Waterfall]
├── Ingestion & Split       [  120ms | 10,000 rows x 15 cols ]
├── CleaningTransformer     [   15ms | 10,000 rows x 15 cols ]
├── MissingValueTransformer [   45ms | 10,000 rows x 15 cols ]
├── EncodingTransformer     [   85ms | 10,000 rows x 38 cols ]
├── ScalingTransformer      [   22ms | 10,000 rows x 38 cols ]
└── XGBoost Estimator       [ 1,450ms | Train accuracy: 0.942 ]

docs.title: Proposed Solution

Live Schema Preview: Upload a sample CSV, inspect inferred column types, and preview transformations live. 3. YAML Synchronizer: Real-time two-way synchronization between visual canvas and the YAML editor. 4. One-Click Run: Trigger pipeline executions with live progress streaming.

docs.text:
This document outlines upcoming architectural enhancements planned for mlflow-experience.

Full Future Capabilities Matrix

For an in-depth exploration of 8 future scenarios (Autonomous Agents, Cloud Lakehouses, Optuna HPO, Production Serving, and Monitoring), read the full Future Enhancements & Scenarios guide.

docs.title: Current Design: Linear Pipeline
docs.text: Currently, the pipeline executes sequentially: $$\text{Step 1} \to \text{Step 2} \to \text{Step 3} \to \text{Step 4}$$

docs.title: Planned Design: DAG Execution
docs.text:
Real-world feature engineering often requires branching (e.g. processing text features and numeric features independently, then merging them before the model):

graph TD
    Raw[Raw Ingestion] --> Clean[Clean & Impute]
    Clean --> NumBranch[Numeric Scaling]
    Clean --> CatBranch[Categorical Encoding]
    NumBranch --> Merge[Merge Features]
    CatBranch --> Merge
    Merge --> Model[Model Estimator]

Key Improvements: - Explicit depends_on definitions in YAML for each node. - Automatic dependency ordering via Topological Sorting. - Cycle detection to prevent infinite loops.

docs.title: Current Design
docs.text: The entire pipeline runs inside one parent MLflow run.

docs.title: Planned Design
docs.text:
Each step in the pipeline automatically creates a nested child run in MLflow:

customer_churn_pipeline (Parent Run)
 ├── rename_columns (Child Run)
 ├── handle_missing (Child Run)
 ├── encode_features (Child Run)
 ├── scale_features (Child Run)
 └── model_fit (Child Run)

By wrapping transformer execution in a @track_node decorator: - Each step automatically logs input shape, output shape, and execution time in milliseconds. - Pinpoints the exact step where an error or data anomaly occurred.

docs.title: 3. Configurable Feature Engineering Factories
docs.text: Formalize src/core/pipelines/features.py into a modular feature generator: - Aggregations: Group-by calculations (e.g. average monthly spend per user). - Interactions: Automated ratio, difference, and product features (e.g. total_spend / tenure). - Temporal Transformations: Sine/Cosine cyclic encoding for dates, day-of-week extraction, and rolling metrics.

docs.title: Error Symptom
docs.text: urllib3.exceptions.MaxRetryError: HTTPConnectionPool(host='localhost', port=5000): Max retries exceeded with url: /api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/get-by-name

docs.title: Why It Happens
docs.text: The pipeline is trying to connect to an MLflow tracking server at http://localhost:5000, but no server is listening on that port.

docs.title: How to Fix
docs.text:
Option A: Start the local MLflow server with uv 

uv run mlflow server --backend-store-uri sqlite:///mlflow.db --default-artifact-root ./mlruns --port 5000

Option B: Start the Docker stack 

docker compose up -d

Option C: Track directly to local disk without a server Edit your YAML configuration to log directly to a local folder: 

mlflow:
  tracking_uri: file:./mlruns

docs.title: Error Symptom
docs.text:
pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for MissingValueConfig
strategy
  Input should be 'mean', 'median', 'mode' or 'constant' [type=literal_error, input_value='average', input_type=str]

docs.title: Why It Happens
docs.text: You used an unsupported strategy name or misspelled a parameter in your YAML file.

docs.title: How to Fix
docs.text: Look at the error message: it tells you the exact field (strategy) and the valid allowed values ('mean', 'median', 'mode' or 'constant'). Update your YAML file accordingly.

docs.title: Error Symptom
docs.text: KeyError: 'Total Spend'

docs.title: Why It Happens
docs.text: You renamed a column in an early preprocessing step, but referenced the old column name in a later step (e.g. imputation, scaling, or encoding).

docs.title: How to Fix
docs.text:
Remember that steps run in sequential order. If you rename "Total Spend" to total_spend, all subsequent steps must use total_spend:

preprocessing:
  - name: rename_columns
    type: rename
    params:
      mapping:
        "Total Spend": total_spend

  - name: scale_features
    type: scaling
    params:
      columns:
        - name: total_spend  # <--- Use the new renamed name here!
          strategy: minmax

docs.title: Why It Happens

docs.title: How to Fix
